utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Miroslav Tadic, Blagoje Simic and Simo Zaric. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic, you're continuing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Lukic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, sir. Good morning to the parties in the proceedings. I would just like for a moment to move into private session so that I could ask the witness two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, we talked -- sir, yesterday, we talked about your stay at Batkovic, about the roll call, the procedure of people being called out to go to the exchange, and now in a minute we will go on to the exchange itself but before that I'm interested in one more topic. In Batkovic, while you were there, were there any stories or talk amongst you detainees about any money for exchanges that any money was required for people to go to an exchange. Was there any talk about whether anybody was given money or whether anybody gave money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, there was talk about that but I think it's impossible amongst all of us, and I think there are about 600 or 700 of us for any of us to be able to give anybody any money without anybody else seeing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear and did any of your acquaintances, the people who were with you at Batkovic, tell you personally that they gave somebody money so that they could be included in the exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear from anyone the name of any person who was asked to give money in order that they could go to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, what happened regarding your exchange? When were you called out? When did this take place? And then I will ask you a couple of questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was the 29th of January, 1993. We were called out and told to pack. We packed and we went outside. They searched us, superficially. There was a bus there from Bijeljina and we set off. We were met by a bus at a certain place that was driving civilians from Samac. When we crossed over --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one moment. When you say Raca, what is Raca, what was that, why did you mention that place? Why did you wait there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the border, Raca is the border between Serbia and Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we crossed over, they took us to Lipovac, we stopped on the right side. We were standing on the right side, those people who were detained and the civilians stopped on the left side. The exchange began. There was a contingent of IFOR there. They were Russians. The exchange began. From our bus, eight people left. Then eight people came from the other side. People of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. Did you see what happened to the civilians? Did they go in groups of eight or did that happen in a different way, the people who were in the other bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They crossed over in an organised manner, because those people were not exchanged for anyone specifically. They just were going into another country. And we continued -- I didn't see where the checkpoint was from the place where I was standing. When it was my turn to go, I told Mr. Tadic, who was standing next to the exit of the bus, I told him that I do not want to go to the exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you got to Tadic, where were you standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were leaving the bus in groups of eight; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, eight by eight, eight people would leave the bus, eight people would come from the other side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those people who were leaving the bus, where were they going? Were they going straight to the other bus or did they go to the checkpoint? Were you able to see the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You couldn't see the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they going in the direction of the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were going in the direction of Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was Tadic standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was standing outside next to the door of the bus. I went up to him and I told him that I didn't want to go to the exchange, to be exchanged. And he literally told me, "if you don't want to, you can stay in the bus." I told him that I heard that I was supposed to go to the line and report to the International Red Cross, that I should tell them if I wanted to go then I should go, I guess Tadic said, "if you don't want to go, stay on the bus, and if you want to go, then go."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to this place, was Miroslav Tadic there all the time or did he go anywhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was standing there the entire time, until the exchange was completed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember was anybody else with him, perhaps from Samac, who was working on the exchanges on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Veljo Maslic was there, and Svetozar? I cannot remember his last name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his nickname?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is a Montenegrin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Sveta Vasovic, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Vasovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, before you went to the exchange, did you hear in Batkovic that anyone was looking for you or did you hear later that anybody was requesting you to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this part that the witness has just talked about now be in private session? Because it relates to the witness's brother. If we can just move into private session so that I could explain for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in public session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, while you were at Batkovic, did you get any information about the people who did not want to go to the exchange, specifically did they stay in Batkovic or did they go home? Did you find out about this procedure while you were still at Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes we knew in Batkovic that if you returned, if you didn't want to go, then you would return home. There weren't too many of us who returned. All of these others left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember the names of anybody who stayed, who didn't wish to leave?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Hasanefendic, Safet, Mijo Radic and a young man, I know him by sight but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened after that when you said that you did not want to go? What happened later?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we all got into the bus, they took us to this motel in Sid, to dinner. At this motel, in the reception area, I was looking around and I saw Mrs. Mirjana Tadic with another woman. She was familiar but I don't remember who it was. She came up to me, greeted me, asked me how I was, then I went to dinner. We had dinner. Then the major told everybody that it will not be possible for all of us to go home that evening, that we had to stay in Bijeljina, of course there were reactions. He said: "No, but we must. Tomorrow you will go."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This major that you mentioned, was that is a military major with a rank of a major?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was Major Simic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Lukic, being that we all know Simic is a very popular name in Bosnia-Herzegovina, this Major Simic, did he have a first name and what was he a major with? Was he JNA, Army of Republika Srpska, what have you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard Judge Williams's question. You mentioned Major Simic's name. Do you know anything more about this man? Do you know his name and do you know which army he's in?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know his name but as far as I heard, he was the commander of the Semberija region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I were to tell you and ask you whether this was a person by the name of Major Jovika Savic? Is that that person? Do you know Jovika Savic, Major is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If I can assist my learned colleague because we have some confusion here in the transcript. Page 9, line 23, it's Major, Jovika. Major is his military rank and Jovika Savic this is the name that we've heard on a number of occasions before this Tribunal, as in charge for exchanges, military exchanges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, it will be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that you were there together at dinner, in Sid, who was there at that dinner? Who did you go to dinner with? Who entered your bus during the exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: People of Serb ethnicity boarded the bus, and we sat next to each other. We weren't thinking about who was who. We simply ate, then we were taken to Bijeljina, spent the night there. In the morning, we were given breakfast. The television came and taped us. We received a questionnaire which we were supposed to fill in, which that man whom I referred to as Simic, he explained it to us nicely. He said, "please, write down everything that you are asked to write down. Don't be afraid of anything. There won't be a hair missing from your head." From the questions, as far as I can recall, they were asking where are you from, who arrested you, who was guarding you, please freely put your names down and I guarantee that no harm will come to you. We filled this out and they even brought a doctor in, if anybody needed anything. And then when all of this was over, we set out for Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go when you came to Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got out in the village of Crkvina. This is five kilometres away from Samac. Because they were supposed to take the ethnic Serbs to Novi Grad and Dubica. Veljo asked us, "do you want to come with us? And then we can return you after that." And we said, "no, we will get out here and we'll find some transportation and go home. We can also walk. I could get home on foot. It's five kilometres." And then a policeman took us, Dragan Stevic. He happened to come by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's not that important for us. So, sir, I'm going to put just a few more questions to you in relation to what we've been discussing. Did anybody tell you, sir, that you had to go to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody tell you that you shouldn't dare go back to your homes in Samac, that there was no place for you there or something like that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody threaten you that you will get in harm's way if you were to return in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was your daughter? Where were your wife and family then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were at home in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Samac? What was your wish?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was born there. Fourth generation in Samac. That's where my family was. I mean, quite simply, I cannot leave Samac. I came back at all costs because I love my town of Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since then, have you been living in your Samac throughout?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions from this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Cross-examination? MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Di Fazio:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you can answer my questions with a yes or a no, it will help to speed things up and make this -- my questioning briefer. Do you know a gentleman named Sabah Seric? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How well do you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him well. He's a relative of mine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was he in Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was in Batkovic while you were in Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long was he in Batkovic for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really say how long he was there exactly but I think it was about a month and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. About a month and a half. Now, you arrived in Batkovic on the 27th of November, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were exchanged in late January, the 29th, I think?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think the correct position is that he was taken to the exchange line because he wasn't exchanged. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, Your Honour is quite correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I misled you there briefly. You were taken to the point of exchange in late January?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your estimation, during the period of time between late November and late January, Sabah Seric may have been in there with you for about a month and a half at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And have you got any idea when Sabah Seric was born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you got any idea about how old he was back then in 1993, early 1993, late 1992, approximately how old he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really say. I don't think I could answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, were both you and your brother arrested in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you arrested simultaneously, both of you at the same time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was arrested first?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My brother.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long after his arrest were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 40 days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you both arrested for the same reason, namely some allegation that you were both firing guns or rifles from the area of your --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just a moment, please. I object. Could we please move into private session, as far as this particular matter is concerned? In view of the facts that are being referred to now in the questions? MR. DI FAZIO: I have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, we can move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were arrested in late June -- late June, I believe?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the 27th of June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were then kept in the SUP, the SUP building, for five months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the SUP building, you witnessed, did you not, daily beatings and torture of the inmates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my time, there was very little. I don't know about before that. Stories were going around but I don't know about before that because we were not there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Just rest assured that I'm not asking you about any other time other than the time when you were there. I'm asking you about your five months. Now, were men beaten with truncheons, kicked with boots, hit and struck with whatever object was available by police, paramilitaries, and any other men who came into the SUP building freely in order to carry out such beatings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 29th of July, the last one happened but it wasn't the kind of hitting that took place before that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. So you're telling the Chamber that in your five months in the SUP building, you know of only one assault on an inmate on the 29th of July? Is that -- am I correct in my understanding?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw no sexual assaults, you saw no teeth being pulled, you saw no blood on the walls, you heard no screams of men crying out from torture, you didn't see Stevan Todorovic daily attacking and assaulting inmates, you saw no such bloody tortured daily routines?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no problem with this question but it has at least ten questions in this one. Perhaps he saw something and some other things. Perhaps he saw blood but never saw anyone pulling the teeth. This is unfair to the witness to pose such a question. MR. DI FAZIO: I don't want to spend a lot of time going over these details. I'm anxious to get this aspect of my cross-examination completed as quickly as possible. The witness, I'm sure, is quite able to differentiate between those matters. If he saw some of those things, and didn't see others, I'm sure he can tell us. It's just a question of efficiency. I don't need to go through each and every item individually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness can answer. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that basic scenario that I just described to you in my question, you didn't see any of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you could ascertain, the men in the SUP who were imprisoned there, they were all Croats and Muslims, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most were Muslims in the period while I was there, because Croats were in the high school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to ascertain in the period of time that you were held in the SUP, or indeed perhaps before you were taken to the SUP building, that there were large-scale arrests of Croat and Muslim men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I worked in a company that is close to my home. I would go from home to work and from work back home so I had no idea what was going on in town, in this other part, and I didn't dare move about because after all there was a war going on, there was a state of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Were men who were held in the SUP desperate to get out of the SUP, as far as you can tell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some people said so. I did not talk about that. I did not even think about an exchange. I mean, on that 27th of November, they took us to Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean you didn't even think of an exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I didn't want to go anywhere from Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the possibility of getting yourself out of the SUP via an exchange discussed amongst prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course. Things like that would be discussed by people who wanted to go. Of course there was such discussion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did any of the men who were held in the SUP, that is, talking about the period of time before you went to Batkovic, were any of the men who were held in the SUP able to leave via an exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period while I was there, as for the people who were detained in the SUP, there was no exchange. It's only from Batkovic that exchanges continued.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I think I -- we should have that question and answer redacted. I asked it before I realised that it may tend to identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see him on any other occasions apart from those two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Between the time your brother was exchanged and your eventual exchange, did you have any communications with your brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He let me know through the International Red Cross that he had returned home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. And was your brother able to tell your relatives elsewhere that he was back safely in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but he probably could have sent a message through the International Red Cross but I know for sure that he did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the day of your release from Batkovic, all that you were told, up until you got to the point of exchange, was to get yourself together, pack your belongings because you were being taken off to the exchange point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told, after our names were called out, "pack up, you're going to go for an exchange." That was it. There were no contacts with anyone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you had not made any moves to seek an exchange?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally had not but I was hoping for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you hoping for it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not get out of Batkovic in any other way, only through an exchange, and crossing the border.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody left that way, not only me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So you're not aware of any prisoners being simply released from Batkovic and allowed to go back home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never saw that happen in the period of time in which you were in Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had not had an opportunity to speak to anyone who had been taken to the exchange point and then declined to cross over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I mean is you, in the time that you were in Batkovic, or indeed even in the SUP, you hadn't had a chance to speak to any man who had been taken to the exchange point and then declined to cross over into Croatia, had decided that he didn't want to cross and come back? You'd spoken to no such people, had you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which period you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the period of time that you were in the SUP and in Batkovic and up until you were taken to the exchange point. In that period of time, you never spoke to any man, woman, who was taken to the exchange point and then returned back to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not have been with them when I was detained. I could not have talked to them either.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. I understand that. And so therefore how can you tell the Chamber that when you were in Batkovic, you knew that you could go home from the exchange point if that's what you decided to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my relative I received a message through the International Red Cross to go to Orasje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This morning, witness, you testified that when you were in Batkovic, you -- all of you men, you prisoners, knew that you could go home, that you could go home back to your homes in Bosanski Samac, if you didn't want to be exchanged at the exchange point. Now, how did you know that? That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone found out from -- from someone. I mean we talked amongst ourselves and that's how we found out that it would be possible to return. In the beginning it wasn't possible to return. This was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone at Batkovic ask the men after they had been assembled on the bus which ones are going to go across at the exchange point and which ones are going to go home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked who wanted to go or if they wanted to go, but simply like I did myself, it was just enough to say that I did not wish to go to -- to be exchanged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these prisoners were never informed by Mr. Tadic on the bus that now that they were being released from Batkovic, it was their choice to cross or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please, could you wait, please? I think that if we wanted to be fair to the witness, this question by the Prosecution can only refer to the moment when he was in the bus. This witness cannot say what was going on in the buses carrying other people unless the question is whether he had heard anything about it because the question here on page 22, line 21, was did anyone at Batkovic, and then it continues. How can this witness know what the procedure was at other exchanges? He can only be asked about his own exchange. MR. DI FAZIO: I was asking about his own exchange.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And on the bus, meaning the bus on which the -- in which the witness was. MR. DI FAZIO: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it's quite specific. MR. DI FAZIO: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, my question is this: Did Mr. Tadic or any other official tell you while you were on the bus, "look, men, now that you have been released, you can just go home to Bosanski Samac"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in those words, nobody said anything to us, but we already knew that and I already told you that I asked Mr. Tadic, I told him that I didn't want to go, and he told me to stay on the bus.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fair enough, but that was at the exchange point. Now I'm talking about the trip between Batkovic and the point of exchange. In that period of time, no one mentioned anything to you about being at liberty to return?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bus is big. I don't know what was talked about. He didn't go from one person to another. But I don't know if he talked to any person in particular.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the exchange point itself, please. Your evidence this morning was that you got up, out of the bus, got out of the bus, Mr. Tadic was next to the door of the bus, and you told us twice this morning, twice, that Mr. Tadic's words to you were: "If you don't want to go, just stay on the bus," correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's what you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you stayed on the bus, and then the bus eventually after all the exchange activities were finished, turned around and you started on your journey back to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First we returned to the motel in Sid for dinner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But that basic procedure that I've just led you through is what happened? You get off the bus. At the bus door Tadic says to you, "if you don't want to go, stay on the bus." You get back on the bus, you wait, then the bus turns around and starts its journey back to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So you did not speak to the ICRC, the International Committee of the Red Cross, nor did you speak to any Croatian officials?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not tell anyone other than Mr. Tadic that it was your decision not to cross over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your relatives wouldn't have received any message from the Croatians, at least the Croatians who were at the exchange site, that it was your desire not to cross?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Objection. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is being asked to speculate whether they received information from the other side. He cannot know something like that unless he was conveyed that in a message. He can be asked whether he received information whether any of them said that he did not wish to go to the exchange. MR. DI FAZIO: I'll withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever tell you why it was necessary to drive you on a bus to the exchange point if you didn't want to cross over? Did anyone explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked amongst ourselves about how we found out that you had to go to the place of exchange.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect, you haven't really answered my question. Did anyone ever tell you why it was necessary to put you on a bus and take you to the exchange point? Didn't anyone tell you, "look, Mr." -- "Look, witness, just go back straight to Bosanski Samac, catch a bus, get a lift, you're free"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody told me that I could go directly to Samac from Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew, didn't you, Witness, that this process of pulling you out of a prison, taking you to the exchange point, was part of a desire to get rid of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This was a normal exchange. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you very much. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Re-examination? Re-examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, we will discuss a little more the topics on which you gave your answers to the Prosecutor. He asked you first about your relative, Sabah Seric. Do you know when he went to the exchange? You said that you did and you answered that question. My question refers to these questions by the Prosecutor. Do you know whether Abdulah Drljacic aka Drke was with you at Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether the two of them left in the same exchange? Do you remember that he also left in the same period as Seric?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The Prosecutor also asked you about the beating and mistreatment and about what you know while you were in the SUP. Specifically for the period while you were there. It's clear already before this Trial Chamber that you were there in the period from late June until late November. You said that you were at the SUP all of the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you were there in that room? Were you in that one room all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the entire period in one room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many of you were in that room? Could you please tell us, in that period generally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At a certain point there were 25 of us. There were Croats also there. Then they would take them away from us, they would separate the Croats from the Muslims, they took the Croats to the school so that the number dropped to about 19.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that period, during those five months while you were in that room, or if you went out of that room, how many times did you personally see beatings and mistreatment? You personally, during that period while you were at the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not one single time with my own eyes. I only heard that people were moaning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the 29th of July, did you see anybody being taken out of your room and returned all bloodied?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the 29th of July, did you see anyone being taken from your room, being beaten and being brought back bloodied to the room or -- and did anyone ever tell you that they were beaten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A neighbour of mine told me that, but there wasn't that much beating. He simply got up and refused to clean the toilet and then he was taken away, he was returned in five minutes. He had a couple of bruises on his face.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this happened just once?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you about what Tadic said when you went to the exchange in that procedure, to the effect that if you don't want to go, you can go home, and the Prosecutor said we already knew that. This is what you told the Prosecutor. My first question is: Did you get information from your brother and you've already told me that, whether he said at the exchange that he did not wish to go, that he returned home and that he is still living in Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wife told me the brother came back and I knew that he would come back because we had agreed on that. MR. DI FAZIO: I assume we are going to get a date and a time for when that information was conveyed. Otherwise the evidence is of no use to you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you get that information, that letter, that information from your wife about what happened to your brother? You don't need to tell us specifically.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime before my exchange, because the messages took a very long time to get to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anybody of the guards perhaps tell you that if anybody did not wish to be exchanged could return? Did anybody tell you something to that effect perhaps? MR. DI FAZIO: [Previous translation continues]... Cross-examination, and the answer is wrapped up like a present for the witness. He couldn't be more leading than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you find out from anyone else, any official, any other person, other than the persons who were detained, receive any kind of information about the exchange procedure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Yes, witness, I just have two small questions for you. You just mentioned, this is page 27, line 16 and 17, concerning beatings and mistreatment in the time you were incarcerated in the SUP, and you say on these lines: "Not one single time with my own eyes. I only heard that people were moaning." My question to you, witness, is: When you say you heard that people were moaning, did you hear this because other people told you about it or did you hear the moaning with your own ears?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the moaning with my own ears because this took place out in the corridor near the door to the room where I was in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, that clarifies that. The second question that I have concerns something mentioned in your statement, in paragraph 16, where it is stated: "On 3rd December, 1992, the International Red Cross came to Batkovic to make a list of us." And what I'm wondering is when the International Red Cross came, do you recall who the representative of the Red Cross was? And secondly, was that person accompanied by anyone from Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they were from France. There was nobody from Bosanski Samac. There was a woman interpreter from Tuzla. She was of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may be allowed to put a question which arises from the questions of Her Honour Judge Williams?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you wait for Judge Lindholm as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, yes, yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: By no means. Sir, I have a couple of minor questions. As we have learned you stayed at the SUP for around five months. That's a rather long time. And I'm interested in how many times you were interrogated during that time. In your written statement, in paragraphs 12 and 13, from those it appears that you were interrogated by inspectors and you name Milos Savic and Simo Bozic. How many times and how often were you interrogated during those five months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Just once, at the beginning, at the beginning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps, after about 40 days. Perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Well, so most of the time you were just detained at the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Did you, during that time, have any possibilities to stay in contact with people outside the SUP?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: So you were completely isolated there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't allow us to keep contacts. I don't know what the reason was. We were in the rooms. Later, they would allow us to go out into the yard to walk around a little bit. Then we would say, "perhaps the corridor needs to be cleaned or the yard," so we would do that to keep busy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you didn't have any possibilities to receive visitors either?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Okay. No further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic? You wanted to ask as a result of the answers from the questions from the bench?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask just one question. Just one question so I get it clear in my head. Further examination by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What Judge Williams asked you about hearing the screaming with your very own ears from the room where you were, did you hear this on several occasions or does this refer just to that 27th of June?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This only refers to the 27th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Tell us what happened on that day so that we all know in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DW8/3 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Antesa succumbed to the beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: One very short question, if you allow me. Were you given any reasons for your transfer from the SUP in Bosanski Samac to Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was said that Batkovic was a safer place because Samac was being shelled. Two detainees were killed by the shells. Also another woman was killed in her own yard, not far from the SUP. And this is why we were being taken to Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LINDHOLM
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you very much for giving evidence to the Tribunal. You are now through. You can leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, while we wait for the next witness if I may address the Trial Chamber for one issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That is related to -- it is related to one of -- one of the witnesses for Mr. Zaric's Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If it can be on private session very briefly I want -- it won't take long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, can we move into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Kuresevic. My name is Phillip Weiner. I'm here on behalf of the Prosecution and I'm going to be asking you some questions this morning. All right? Sir, you indicated that you received a mobilisation summons and I have to assume in late 1991, early, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: After doing their military service, all men in the former Yugoslavia, were deployed in the reserve force of the military. After I did my military service, I was assigned to some kind of reconnaissance, sabotage unit. In the beginning of 1992, I did not consider this to be mobilisation. I only thought that I was being reassigned to another unit which was called the 4th Detachment, but all right, let it be, let the 4th Detachment be called mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't sent to the TO, Territorial Defence, rather you were sent to the 4th Detachment, isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You became a member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was a member of that unit, and I was assigned commander of a company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you received a weapon? An automatic rifle, sir, as part of your assignment to the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I was given weapons later when we went out for an exercise. That is when we were issued weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And prior to that, you'd been a reserve, I believe, captain and you were involved in reconnaissance -- in a reconnaissance and sabotage unit?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: No. I was not a reserve captain before. I had the lowest NCO rank in the military and now be careful, rank in terms of establishment is a special definition. I did not get an official rank but during the war, I was deployed to a post where the rank of captain was required so then I only got this rank of captain by way of establishment, but this was only in 1993-94.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Sorry, it wasn't clear in your statement. Now, sir, you indicated that you attended the 4th Detachment meeting at memorial hall, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you learn at that time or sometime later that Simo Zaric was an assistant commander and that the defendant Miroslav Tadic was also an assistant commander in the 4th Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I know that Simo Zaric was in the command. Now, who did what is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you aware that Miroslav Tadic was also in the command?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: People talked about that, but I was not duty-bound to know the actual establishment of the command and I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were advised at that meeting of the objectives of the 4th Detachment which was to defend the town against any or all paramilitary groups, isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know, sir, that on the 17th of April, and the days that followed, the 4th Detachment did not meet this objective?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The 4th Detachment -- I mean on the 17th of April, although I was commander of a company, according to the establishment, before -- well, let's say the war I did not know anything that was going on, even on the 17th of April, my company or rather this group of people that I was supposed to command did not have any activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's take it step by step. You learned sometime after the 17th of April, whether it's the 17th, 18th, 19th, 20th, that Serbian forces had taken over the vital buildings and facilities in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what it means that a Serb vital buildings and facilities were taken over by Serb buildings or did I misunderstand the interpretation? This is the interpretation that I got actually that Serb buildings took Serb facilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you learn during the 17th or the week following that Serb forces, the Serb police that Todorovic brought in, the Serb paramilitaries or volunteers that came into Samac, had taken over the vital buildings and facilities such as the municipal building, the police department, the TO, the radio station, the silos?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I knew that practically war had started, and that there was some kind of information and that things had changed. There was shooting in town and now, as for these details, which facilities were under whose control and in their entirety, that is something I don't know. I had a special role. I was director of a company. So --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you eventually learn that Serb forces had taken over the town?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you learned that obviously the town of Samac had been taken over?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I learned that the town of Samac had had a government administration instituted in it, that it had been changed in some way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. That it was now a Serbian Municipality of Samac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what they called it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That a -- that the elected government was no longer in power, the government that was elected in 1990 was no longer in power?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: The government that had been elected in 1990 functioned until just before the war. I don't know. A month or two or three previously. I don't know to which extent. I mean, I as director had some problems, a bit of a problem, because this government was based on a coalition between the Serbs, Croats and Muslims. Some of the assemblymen, some of the people who were in government had left the government and it did not really function properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But after April 17th, that elected government was no longer in power because there was now a new Serb municipality of Samac, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I think there were changes. I mean, I know there were changes. Now, who participated in this, whether somebody from the old government took part in the new government is something that I cannot guarantee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you were aware that there was now a Crisis Staff in Bosanski Samac that was in control?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I knew, I had information that there was a Crisis Staff, but on the whole, I didn't know what its role was and until the present day, I do not know what it did or rather what all the things it did were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And sir, sometime after April 17th, you've learned that the SDS president or the president of the SDS party, the defendant Blagoje Simic, was now the Crisis Staff president?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were a member of the SDP party, and as a member of the SDP party and a Yugoslav, you didn't want a Serb-controlled or SDS-controlled municipality of Samac, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: A political party strives for certain objectives or rather it has certain objectives and it disagrees with other political parties in several segments. One of these segments is this ethnic makeup or let us put it this way, taking into consideration the entire population. But a political party has its objectives, its plans, in the economy, in the non-economic sector, in all areas and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But my question is: As a member, as a Yugoslav that believes in multi-ethnicity, as a member of the SDP which was a multi-ethnic party, you did not want a Serb-controlled or a SDS-controlled municipality, a municipality controlled by one ethnic group, you didn't want that, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. I didn't want a municipality that would be under the control of one ethnic group only, and I did not want only one ethnic group to be in that municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's go back to April 17th and the days that followed. You know that the JNA and the 4th Detachment did not remove this new Crisis Staff. You knew that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I did not take part in that particular section. I did not take part in that with the 4th Detachment and I don't know exactly who did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Sir, my question is: The 4th Detachment and the JNA did not remove this new Serbian Crisis Staff led by Dr. Blagoje Simic. They never did that, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also know that the 4th Detachment and the JNA did not reinstate the former democratically elected government?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also know that the JNA and the 4th Detachment did not put an end to this new Serb municipality which had been formed or established?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I've already answered that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also know that the JNA and the 4th Detachment did not remove those Serbian paramilitaries or volunteers in camouflage uniforms that came into the municipality?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know that too. They did not lock them up.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know instead the 4th Detachment or certain units of the 4th Detachment were sent to guard the river banks, to protect the municipality, the Serbian municipality, against attack, not your unit but other units were sent to guard the river banks. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I think before the war, I went to Croatia and vehicles from my company always went to Croatia and this is how I understood it, that there is a possibility of an attack coming from Croatia because there had already been bunkers there and the military was there already and now what units took part in this, which segments of the 4th Detachment took part in this is something that I don't know. Other people know about that better.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your unit wasn't even activated. They didn't call you and ask you to go and protect the river banks, protect any buildings, protect the Serbian community?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you agree that by the 4th Detachment's lack of response to this Serbian takeover, it ensured its survival?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand this. What does it mean? Whose survival?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By protecting the river banks and protecting against an attack the 4th Detachment ensured the survival of this new Serbian municipality?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I think that the 4th Detachment protected the town from attacks coming from the Croatian side, from the side of the Republic of Croatia, and it protected the town from attacks from any units in Bosnia, on the Croatian territory in Prud, units had already been established, also in Orasje, there were units that had been formed in Gradacac, I knew all of that because people who worked in my company talked about this. And the night before the war, I was returning from Obudovac, and at a crossroads, near Samac, I was stopped by the police that had Croatian insignia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But sir, by protecting the river banks and protecting against attack, the 4th Detachment defended this new Serbian municipality against any attack, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was defending the whole population in that municipality. The task of the 4th Detachment was not to defend the authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was by defending the river banks they were defending the new municipality, the Serbian Municipality of Samac and Pelagicevo under formation, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the 4th Detachment was defending the territory of the municipality. That was the objective. Its objective was not to defend Blagoje or Mato or Anto or anybody who was in the government there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But sir, you have to agree, and you've testified, the 4th Detachment did not respond to the Serbian takeover of Samac. They did not remove the new Crisis Staff and they did not remove the paramilitaries. That was your testimony, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you know who Milan Simic is?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know that at sometime in May, Milan Simic became president of the executive board in Samac?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: When he became the president of the executive board, I don't know, but I know that he was president of the executive board.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're also aware that he has pled guilty in this Court to torturing non-Serb prisoners in the primary school at Samac. Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: If he tortured the non-Serb population in Samac, and if he stated that, then that must be so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: And if he admitted his guilt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. He has admitted his guilt, and as part of his admission n paragraph 30 of the 4th amended indictment which is referred to on page 5 of the sentencing judgement, he states, "Bosnia and Herzegovina declared its independence from Yugoslavia on 29 February, 1992. Long before this, however, the SDS and the JNA had been making plans for the probability of a war which included the creation of separate Serb-controlled municipalities throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina." Were you aware, sir, of these SDS and JNA plans?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that. Neither was I supposed to know that. And I don't believe that such plans existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware of the coordination and the cooperation between the SDS, the Serb leaders and the JNA prior to and during the war?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Please, could you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, were you aware of the cooperation and coordination of activities between the SDS, the JNA and the Serb leaders in Bosnia-Herzegovina prior to the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what kind of contacts they were. I was doing my job. My job was the economy. In the political sense, I contacted with the representatives of the HDZ, the SDS and the SDA. All three parties were politically oriented, let's put it that way, against our party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you're familiar with the person named Biljana Plavsic?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know she was an SDS and Serb leader in Bosnia-Herzegovina? A member of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I know that there was a leadership of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you agree that Biljana Plavsic was in a better position than you as one of the leaders and as a president of the SDS to be aware of any relationship between the SDS and the JNA? Would you agree with me about that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: She probably knew, not probably but she certainly knew those relationships much better than I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you aware as part of her plea to persecution of the non-Serb population in Bosnia-Herzegovina, she has admitted to collaboration between the JNA and the SDS and the Serb leaders of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that those three groups collaborated to persecute the non-Serb population? Are you aware of her admission to that?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I know that she admitted to the guilt -- to being guilty as for what she's charged with but exactly to what, I don't know but I know that she was sentenced for the things that she had committed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the fact that Biljana Plavsic, a national Serb and SDS leader has admitted to collaboration between the JNA and SDS and a local Serb leader, Milan Simic has admitted to collaboration between the SDS and the JNA, isn't that consistent with what you saw in Bosanski Samac where the 4th Detachment and the JNA took no action to remove the Serb paramilitaries, to overthrow this new Crisis Staff which appointed itself? Isn't that consistent, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: This question -- it's not possible to answer it with a yes or no. If it really was the way that you are presenting it to me, then I would be completely wrong for being in Samac. I was in Samac during the war, not because I wanted to remove the non-Serb population, and I participated in the war, but I didn't participate in that war because I wanted to expel any population and to have non-Serb -- the population leave the -- this land. I participated in the war in order to defend my family, to defend my territory, my wife, who is a Croat, to defend my two daughters-in-law who are Croats. That's why.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you're aware, or are you aware that Biljana Plavsic has indicated that she -- that the SDS -- I'm sorry, that the SDS, the Serb leaders, and the JNA collaborated to remove the non-Serb population from Bosnia-Herzegovina? Are you aware of her admission to that? And she's pled guilty to that. Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I believe that I do not seem a bit crazy to you. I'm an intellectual who understands certain questions very well and I've already responded to that question. There is it no need for you to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, the fact that these people said these things, isn't that consistent with the inaction of the JNA? You were never called up, sir, to remove the Serb forces that had come into the community and taken it over. You were never called up to remove the new Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. This is the third or fourth time that the Prosecutor, as part of the same topic, is asking practically the same question, whether the witness knew about the collaboration between the SDS and the JNA, but the witness has responded that he doesn't know anything about that and that he cannot say anything about that but we have already spent half an hour on this topic and the witness is constantly repeating the same answers while the Prosecutor is constantly putting practically identical questions to him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will repeat what I've already said in response to the question of the Prosecutor. Mr. Prosecutor, sir, I've told you that I, as a member of a unit of the JNA, was in Samac in order to defend the citizens of Samac from attacks from the outside, from attacks from Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were never called up to defend them, though, you weren't even activated on the 17th, 18th, 19th or 20th, isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: If it's possible to do that without the index finger, please don't threaten me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not -- sir, I'm not threatening you. I want you to answer my question, sir. And my question is as follows: You were not activated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner, the witness did understand that to be a threat but just avoid doing it. Just ask the questions while you are standing in your place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. It was no threat, Your Honour. Believe me, it was no threat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you were not called up --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: But I understood it as a threat. In my area, when somebody makes this gesture, then it can be very dangerous. Please don't do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry if it upset you, sir. But I'd like you to answer my questions. We have limited amount of time and I'd like you to answer the question that you're asked and my question to you is: You were not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner can I just assure the witness, Mr. Kuresevic, it's unfortunate that that did happen but do understand that you are very, very free where you are sitting to answer the questions of the Prosecutor as you understand them and as you know the facts, so do not feel threatened at all. The questions may go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not activated to take any action, you or the members of your command, were not activated to take any action --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You were not activated and asked to take any action on April 17th, 18th or 19th, either yourself or any members of your command to remove the Serb paramilitaries, to remove the Serb Crisis Staff, which had had taken power or any one who had taken over the town of Bosanski Samac, isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, sir, I'm explaining to you for the fourth time the same thing, and that is we were called to defend Samac, to defend the town, and to defend the citizens of the town, and this is the function that we were performing. That was our function.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was not my question, sir. My question was on the 17th, 18th or 19th, you weren't sent to the river banks, weren't sent to guard any building, you weren't sent out to do anything, either you or members of your command. Or were you? Tell me if you --

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Just one second. I said that this was my unit. That unit is a company of 30 men or 22 men. I, as a commander of that company, was not directed to such tasks, probably I was told from the command that I had other obligations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, sir, the fact that you didn't -- you weren't ordered to take any action to overthrow the -- that government that had -- that had inserted itself into power, to remove the Serbian paramilitaries, that is consistent with Milan Simic's testimony -- I'm sorry, Milan Simic's statement, and Biljana Plavsic's statement that there was a plan between the SDS and the JNA. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I was ordered to go to the company where I worked and in that company --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before the witness continues, Mr. Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the Prosecutor is trying to confuse the witness because there are a lot of questions here. The Prosecutor first should ask the witness whether he knew whether Milan Simic was part of the local SDS, whether he knew whether Biljana Plavsic was in the Presidency, whether he knew how the authorities in government were elected and then only after putting such questions could he ask him these other questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Vukovic, at the beginning of the Prosecution's questions referring to Mr. Milan Simic and Mrs. Biljana Plavsic, the Prosecution did state who these people were. So the witness does understand who these people were and what they had said, according to the questions of the Prosecutor. So the Prosecutor can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, once again, were you sent to your company, you were not given orders to overthrow the new government, you were not given orders to remove the Serb volunteers or paramilitaries, that is consistent with Milan Simic's admission and Biljana Plavsic's admission that there was a plan between the JNA and the SDS to establish Serb municipalities. Isn't that consistent with that? I'm not asking you what you've done. Just isn't that consistent?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I've already answered to this three times or four or five. I don't know that. I told you I cannot know what Biljana, Simic and what Biljana Plavsic and Milan Simic did. I know what we did and what I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir my question is not whether or not you agree with what Biljana Plavsic said, not whether or not you agree with what Milan Simic said but the information that I read out to you that Biljana Plavsic said and that Milan Simic said, that they had coordinated with the JNA, that they had collaborated with the JNA, isn't that consistent with your not receiving orders to take over the town because according to them, there has long been a plan to establish Serb municipalities and that they coordinated with the JNA, the SDS, the Serb leaders. Isn't that consistent with what happened in Samac? Because you weren't given the orders, "remove these paramilitaries". You weren't given the orders, "remove this government that just appointed itself". Isn't that consistent with what they said, not whether you agree with it or not but isn't that consistent with what Simic said and Plavsic said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, the witness has been through this question and he has said what he can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But he's not answering it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the point. Can we move on? He won't give you the answer you want. He has understood the questions and he has given his answers and we've been on this for quite sometime now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If he's not going to answer it the Court should answer it. That's why he's here. He's not here to give political speeches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think he's giving political speeches he's explaining the way he understood things to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But he's not answering the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: On the other hand, these are the sorts of conclusions the Prosecution will be able to draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I disagree, but if that's the Court's view I will move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, please do move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you served as a director in the Master company or Master enterprise, isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that a state-owned transport and trade enterprise?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, for transport, for transport and trade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after April 17th, and this new Serb municipality was established and a new Crisis Staff was established by Blagoje Simic, the defendant in this case, you had to deal with them, you had to take orders from them, isn't that correct, since you were a state-owned company?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't receive orders; as a director, I had certain authority. If there were any changes, these changes were -- in these changes, the directors as a rule do not cooperate directly with the leadership of the municipality, but they communicate and have contact with people who are in charge of such jobs in this period. A person who had contacts with me was the man who was in charge of the economy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you had to deal with the Crisis Staff and the executive board and particularly Milan Simic, the new Samac authorities, isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MARKO KURESEVIC
utterances.text: In the beginning, it wasn't Mr. Milan Simic. I didn't have any contacts with the Crisis Staff because this -- because there was no need for that. There was a different way. As a rule, directors, if necessary, communicate with the executive authorities, with the executive board, or with the person who does not necessarily have to be a member of the executive board but is in charge of the economy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, let me refresh your recollection. Let me show you a letter you received from the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness a letter with ERN number 0061-3077. We just found this in a second letter yesterday as we were doing some research on this witness. We've provided them to Defence counsel and one of these two documents is referred to within the witness's statement, and we've requested English translations. I'll have the witness read it out to us, if the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vukovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VUKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we've only received this today at the break. It's evident that the Prosecution has had this document for a long time. We don't know how they received it, where did they get it from and when and we need to check this document before it's shown to the witness. So we object to having this document shown to the witness today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has already been shown the document by counsel. I gave it to counsel earlier. He has shown the documents, both documents to the witness, without any objection from us. And the witness is familiar with both documents, for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
